turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - cdft_piezo_d_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `d_ij` (the
    piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij|, in pC/N).
  - cdft_piezo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose
    properties are NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the LARGEST
piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij| (in pC/N), then select the 5 best
candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The largest piezoelectric responses in the training set arise from a small number of recurrent structural/chemical motifs: (i) polar tetrahedral sulfides of the Na3SbS4/TaTl3S4 type (d ~ 130–150 pC/N), (ii) lone-pair-driven polar perovskites such as RbPbBr3 (d ~ 154 pC/N), and (iii) selected half-Heusler phases (KYSn, BaAuCl; d ~ 60–70 pC/N).  

Candidate c043 (K3SbS4) is isostructural with the two highest-sulfide examples and is therefore expected to be the strongest.  
Candidates c025, c026 and c041 are polar Ge(II) chloride perovskites whose displacements and chemistry closely parallel RbPbBr3; they form the next tier.  
Candidate c004 (LiMgP) adopts the same half-Heusler setting that produces the 60–70 pC/N responses and completes the top five.  

All other pool entries are either centrosymmetric, chemically dissimilar to the high-d training examples, or belong to families whose training analogues lie well below 40 pC/N.

Final: c043, c025, c041, c026, c004
